  <p class="advent-day-kicker">THE CONTEXT · 5 MINUTES</p>
  <h1 class="advent-day-title">What information does the model have?</h1>
  <p class="advent-day-lead">Yesterday, we saw that the model computes a distribution for the next token. But that distribution depends on a precise input: <strong>the prefix available to the model at that moment</strong>.</p>
</div>

## The question

Which information can condition the next prediction?

## The core idea

At a given step, the model's **immediate context** is the token prefix actually supplied to it. The next token to predict comes after that prefix; it is not part of the context yet.

During generation, the selected token is appended to the prefix. It then becomes available at the next step. The model computes a new distribution conditioned on this extended context.

## Follow an example

<ol class="advent-prefix-steps">
  <li><span class="advent-step-label">Supplied prefix</span><strong>The cat</strong><small>This text is the current context.</small></li>
  <li><span class="advent-step-label">Prediction</span><strong>A distribution for the next token</strong><small>The model does not yet know which continuation will be selected.</small></li>
  <li><span class="advent-step-label">Illustrative selection</span><strong>sleeps</strong><small>Suppose the decoding rule selects this token.</small></li>
  <li><span class="advent-step-label">New prefix</span><strong>The cat sleeps</strong><small>“sleeps” is now part of the context for the next step.</small></li>
</ol>

The second computation therefore does not start from the same context: the prefix has grown. The model parameters can remain unchanged; the conditioning input has changed.

<div class="advent-note">
  **A terminology note.** Here, “context” means only the model's immediate input at a given step. Designing an application context — instructions, retrieved documents, memory, or conversation history — is a broader topic covered in the [context engineering](context-engineering.qmd) lesson.
</div>

## Check yourself

The supplied prefix is now “The cat sleeps”. Is “sleeps” still the next token to predict?

<details class="advent-answer">
<summary>Show the answer</summary>

No. “sleeps” is already part of the supplied prefix. The model computes a distribution for the token that follows “The cat sleeps”.

</details>

## Takeaway

The context is the prefix available at the time of computation. A future token is not part of it until it has been supplied or fed back into the sequence.
